items.title: 9.7 Motion of charged particles in a uniform electric field

blocks.text: Two oppositely charged parallel metal plates produce a uniform electric field between them, directed from the positive to the negative plate. A positive charge +q placed in the field moves in the direction of the field, whereas a negative charge -q moves opposite to it. The magnitude of the electric force acting on a charge q (Fig. 9.17) is F = qE ... (9.26), where E is the electric intensity of the uniform field. If V is the potential difference between the plates and d is their separation, E = V/d ... (9.27).

blocks.alt: Two parallel plates a distance d apart are joined to a battery of voltage V. Between them a positive charge is pushed down towards the negative plate and a negative charge is pushed up towards the positive plate. The caption gives E = V / d.
blocks.caption: Charges between plates connected to a battery (original diagram after Figure 9.17).

blocks.text: To understand the effect of a uniform electric field on the motion of charged particles, consider an electron placed between the two plates. The electron accelerates towards the positive plate due to the force F acting on it. Let V = 20 V and d = 2.0 cm = 2 x 10^-2 m; then E = V/d = 20 V/(2 x 10^-2 m) = 1000 N C^-1. The acceleration of the electron follows from F = ma: a = F/m = qE/m. With q = e = 1.6 x 10^-19 C and m = 9.1 x 10^-31 kg, a = (1.6 x 10^-19 C x 1000 N C^-1)/(9.1 x 10^-31 kg) = 1.76 x 10^14 m s^-2.

If the electron is released from the negative plate, the velocity gained when it reaches the positive plate can be found from the third equation of motion, 2aS = vf^2 - vi^2, with S = d = 2 x 10^-2 m, vi = 0 and vf = v: 2 x 1.76 x 10^14 m s^-2 x 2 x 10^-2 m = v^2, so v^2 = 7.04 x 10^12 m^2 s^-2 (printed without the power of ten) and v = 2.65 x 10^6 m s^-1.

blocks.caption: Electron between plates (V = 20 V, d = 2.0 cm)

blocks.prompt: An electron enters a uniform field E = 300 N C^-1 with vi = 2.99 x 10^6 m s^-1; the plates are 10.0 cm long. Find its acceleration and the time it takes to pass through the field (numerical 9.5).
blocks.explanation: a = eE/m = 1.6 x 10^-19 x 300/9.1 x 10^-31 = 5.27 x 10^13 m s^-2 (opposite to E, hence the print's negative sign). The horizontal velocity is unchanged, so t = 0.100/2.99 x 10^6 = 3.34 x 10^-8 s.

items: Between oppositely charged plates the field is uniform, + to -; positive charges move along E, negative against it. F = qE (9.26), E = V/d (9.27), a = qE/m.
20 V across 2.0 cm: E = 1000 N C^-1, a = 1.76 x 10^14 m s^-2, and an electron from rest reaches the positive plate at 2.65 x 10^6 m s^-1.
